To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
puromycin inhibits the synthesis of DNA by preventing the synthesis of a specific protein which is required for the initiation of DNA synthesis.
the initiation of DNA synthesis in mammalian cells is dependent on protein synthesis.
the synthesis of protein and of DNA in HeLa cells is initiated by a focalized event, and that the initiation of DNA synthesis is accompanied by an increased rate of protein synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular events which occur during the replication cycle of mammalian cells.
the initiation of DNA synthesis and its relationship to the replication process.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the replication of DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the replication of DNA is a focalized event in mammalian cells.
the synthesis of protein is required for the initiation of the duplication of DNA, whereas DNA synthesis itself is independent of the synthesis of protein.
the replication of DNA in the cell is not a continuous process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DNA synthesis in the mammalian cells can be divided into two phases: (a) the initiation phase which requires localized protein synthesis and (b) the elongation phase which is independent of protein synthesis.
the replication process in mammalian cells is a complex one and that the initiation of this process involves the synthesis of a protein which in turn is required for the replication of the DNA.
the synthesis of proteins is required for the initiation of DNA synthesis in mammalian cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the initiation of DNA synthesis is not a simple event but rather requires the coordinated action of many components of the cell.
DNA replication is not a continuous process.
the synthesis of new proteins is required for DNA replication to start.
